2

4	adds no UDL syntax. The runtime prepares exact local inputs and verifies retained
5	records; callers supply actual observations and criterion judgments. Preparation,
6	measurement, declared review, host viewing evidence and engine execution are distinct.
7	
8	## API and publication
9	
10	`prepare(folder, expected, candidate_id, packet_id, options, root=None)` requires a
11	saved raster X with a matching F owner and C, saved owner task and required Q.
12	`folder` must be a project subdirectory; root defaults to its parent. `expected`
13	is the current canonical state hash. IDs must be valid PIXL identifiers, fresh,
14	and leave enough of the 96-character limit for generated suffixes.
15	
16	Options are closed: required `references` (distinct local S/X IDs; `[]` is explicit),
17	`scale` (integer 2..16), `backgrounds` (nonempty distinct `#RRGGBB` or `checkerboard`);
18	optional `max_side` (64..2048, default 1024), `contexts` (default []). Contexts require
19	explicit `source_frame`. Options impose no universal artistic rules.
20	
21	Each context is one of these closed objects, with a distinct nonempty name and a
22	source ID in the candidate plus explicit references:
23	
24	```json
25	{"name":"walk","kind":"frames","source":"candidate","source_frame":0,
26	 "rects":[[0,0,16,16],[16,0,16,16]],"durations_ms":[100,null],
27	 "pivots":[[8,15],null]}
28	```
29	
30	`source_frame` selects an existing zero-based decoded source frame, even for static
31	images. Rectangles are ordered `[x,y,width,height]`, with nonnegative integer origins,
32	positive dimensions and complete containment in that frame. `durations_ms` and
33	`pivots` have exactly the same length as `rects`; duration entries are positive
34	integer milliseconds or null, pivots are local in-bounds integer `[x,y]` or null.
35	Unknown values remain null. Individual frames and a comparison strip are retained.
36	The strip uses common-pivot alignment only if every pivot is known; otherwise it
37	uses top-left sequential placement. Timing observations do not create animation.
38	
39	```json
40	{"name":"neighborhood","kind":"tiles","source":"candidate","source_frame":0,
41	 "tile_size":[16,16],"grid":[[0,1],[2,3]]}
42	```
43	
44	Tile dimensions are positive integers and must divide the selected source exactly.
45	The nonempty rectangular grid is an array of top-to-bottom rows, with left-to-right
46	entries; each integer is a zero-based row-major source tile index. The declared
47	neighborhood is retained with exact RGBA placement. Every horizontal and vertical
48	neighbor pair reports differing adjacent RGBA edge-pixel counts, never an automatic
49	seam verdict. Boolean and fractional values are not valid integer fields.
50	
51	Public adapters use the same request semantics:
52	
53	```text
54	inspection-prepare STORE CANDIDATE PACKET OPTIONS_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT
55	inspection-review STORE PACKET REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT
56	inspection STATE [PACKET] --root ROOT
57	```
58	
59	CLI JSON arguments are local JSON file paths. MCP root is the configured project
60	root, and the closed tool envelopes are:
61	
62	```json
63	{"tool":"pixl_inspection","arguments":{"path":".pixl/state.px","packet_id":"packet"}}
64	{"tool":"pixl_inspection_prepare","arguments":{"store":".pixl","expect":"HASH","candidate_id":"candidate","packet_id":"packet","options":{"references":[],"scale":8,"backgrounds":["#ffffff"]}}}
65	{"tool":"pixl_inspection_review","arguments":{"store":".pixl","expect":"HASH","packet_id":"packet","review_id":"review","observation":{}}}
66	```
67	
68	`packet_id` is optional only for `pixl_inspection`; the other shown argument keys
69	are required. The review's observation placeholder must be replaced by the complete
70	closed review object described below.
71	
72	Source bytes are captured once and checked against their saved hashes before rendering.
73	Every encoded input, decoded frame, native transparent view, native background view,
74	integer-nearest enlarged background view and requested context is retained. Large views
75	use complete logical crops before enlargement. Packet preparation creates auxiliary
76	X records of kind `reference` for inputs/views and a kind `report` X for its JSON.
77	It changes no nomination, task status, E or V. Publication uses ordinary store CAS;
78	failed publication may leave unreferenced immutable files, as with existing delivery.
79	
80	The closed manifest keys are `version` (integer 1), `kind` (`packet`), `packet`,
81	`candidate`, `output`, `task`, `created_at` (timezone-aware timestamp),
82	`source_state_sha256`, `records`, `rendering`. Each original semantic record has
83	exactly `id`, `kind`, `fields` (lossless codec tagged JSON), `sha256` (record hash).
84	The original semantic proof scope includes the candidate, output, contract, required
85	criteria, explicit references and their semantic dependencies. Mutable task/project
86	workflow records are excluded by `graph.proof_scope`; task identity is retained.
87	
88	`rendering` has exactly `inputs`, `views`, `measurements`, `options`,
89	`context_observations`. Inputs have `source`, `path`, `sha256`, `id`. Views add `id`
90	to the renderer's `path`, `source`, `frame`, `context`, `scale`, `background`, `crop`,
91	`width`, `height`, `sha256`. Paths inside the manifest are relative to its directory.
92	IDs are `PACKET.input.N` and `PACKET.view.N`, zero-based in deterministic render order.
93	Files live at `STORE/inspections/MANIFEST_SHA256/`; the report is `manifest.json`.
94	Views returned to a host have project-relative paths, ready for a root-confined viewer.
95	
96	Packet X metadata is closed and typed: `inspection=packet` (Symbol), `version=1`,
97	`candidate` (Ref), `scope` (ordered original semantic Refs), `files` (ordered retained
98	input then view Refs). Auxiliary X metadata is `inspection=file` (Symbol), `source`
99	(Ref). The loader checks original bodies/hashes, ownership, semantic scope, typed
100	projection, canonical manifest bytes and every retained file. It deterministically
101	re-renders retained inputs to validate all nested rendering metadata and exact bytes.
102	This intentionally trades read cost for a complete closed rendering check.
103	
104	Renderer ceilings apply equally to preparation and retained packet verification:
105	64 MiB/source, 256 MiB aggregate sources, 16,384 decoded pixels/axis, 16,777,216 pixels
106	per frame, 1,024 frames/source, 67,108,864 aggregate decoded pixels, 65,536 exact visible
107	colors/frame, 4,096 views, 2,048 delivered pixels/axis, 64 MiB/encoded view,
108	512 MiB aggregate returned files and 134,217,728 rendered pixels. The 65,537th visible
109	color rejects instead of truncating. Manifests additionally have the codec's 16 MiB
110	limit. Context-specific limits remain those documented by the renderer.
111	
112	Prepare returns store `revision`, `hash`, `state`, plus `packet`, `manifest`, `views`,
113	`measurements`, `criteria`, `files_verified:true`. Criterion entries have `id`, `name`,
114	`check`, `domain`, `mode`, `status`, `verdict`. Missing verdicts are `unperformed`.
115	
116	## Explicit review
117	
118	`review(folder, expected, packet_id, review_id, observation, root=None)` requires
119	fresh IDs and current retained bindings. A done task must first be reopened. The
120	closed observation object requires `reviewer`, `observed_at`, `observations`,
121	`verdicts`, `next_action`, `limitations`. Reviewer names a saved A; observation time
122	must have an explicit UTC offset and lie between preparation and local recording.
123	This is caller-declared time, not an attestation that viewing happened.
124	
125	Each observation has exactly `view`, `delivered_size`, `note`. View IDs must belong to
126	this packet and cannot repeat. Dimensions are two positive integers or null. Null
127	means the host has not established dimensions; never copy file dimensions into an
128	unknown host delivery. Notes and next action are nonempty text; limitations is a
129	list of nonempty strings, which may be empty.
130	
131	Each verdict has exactly `criterion`, `status`, `reason`, `supersedes`. Criteria must
132	be distinct and required by this packet's original output. Reasons are nonempty.
133	Local criteria accept pass/fail; engine-domain or live-mode criteria accept only
134	unavailable, without E. Visual/continuity or visual-mode failures need at least one
135	observed candidate-source view; viewing only references cannot establish a candidate
136	failure. Visual/continuity or visual-mode passes require every prepared view, including reference and
137	context native/enlarged variants, observed at its prepared dimensions. Unknown or
138	resized deliveries cannot satisfy complete coverage. This verifies declaration
139	consistency; actual viewing transcripts remain separate evidence. Mechanical criteria
140	with local evidence mode do not require image-view coverage. Their verdicts still
141	require an explicit caller judgment against the saved criterion; measurements are
142	not automatically promoted to verdicts.
143	
144	`supersedes` is null if no current V exists; otherwise it must name that exact current
145	V for this candidate/criterion. The operation marks that V obsolete and retains it.
146	It creates `REVIEW.verdict.N` for each declaration and `REVIEW.evidence.N` for each
147	performed criterion. E binds the exact original candidate/Q scope plus packet, review
148	and all retained files. It uses the criterion's required mode and declared outcome.
149	The saved-plan ordering and ordinary graph/store gates remain authoritative.
150	Omitted criteria stay unperformed unless they already have an existing current V.
151	A separate candidate inherits no V. Task nomination and status are unchanged.
152	
153	Review JSON has exactly `version:1`, `kind:review`, `packet`, `review`, `recorded_at`,
154	`source_state_sha256`, `observation`, `coverage`. Its report X metadata is exactly
155	`inspection=review` (Symbol), `version=1`, `packet` (Ref). Coverage has `complete`,
156	`observed`, `missing`, `resized`, `unknown_size`; ID lists are sorted. Review returns
157	store commit fields plus `packet`, `review`, `verdicts` (new IDs), `coverage`,
158	`files_verified:true`. Retained next actions and limitations remain in observation.
159	
160	## Cold reporting and history
161	
162	`report(doc, root, packet_id=None)` returns `hash`, `files_verified:true`, `packets`.
163	Each packet has identity/ownership/time, views, measurements, context observations,
164	original criteria text with current candidate verdicts, `binding_drift` (changed
165	original semantic IDs), retained `reviews`, `files_verified:true`,
166	`visual_quality_verified:false`, `engine_import_verified:false`. Those final flags
167	state the runtime's limits; declared caller verdicts are represented separately.
168	
169	Proper amendments remain readable with original criterion text; new reviews against
170	stale packets are rejected. Earlier E/V must be superseded under existing rules when
171	amending their dependencies. Reporting validates even obsolete inspection E against
172	its original retained closure and validates review V projections. Closed equivalence
173	preserves exact scalar types: booleans cannot stand in for integers and fractional
174	JSON representations cannot replace integer rendering metadata. Retained reads enforce
175	remaining aggregate source-byte limits before reading each input. Relocation is safe
176	when the project and its relative store layout are copied together.
177	
178	These guarantees belong to the inspection APIs. Ordinary generic X records remain
179	mutable under existing semantics; arbitrary generic edits are not inspection
180	publication. The loader detects inconsistent retained files, bodies and projections;
181	it does not establish cryptographic authorship or guarantee discovery after arbitrary
182	coordinated generic rewriting. Historical receipts are never edited to imply new tests.
